title: Moving to the UK?: UK’s New Immigration Policies Explained!
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: To make rules, controls, or conditions stricter or harder to meet.
A UK immigration status that allows a person to live and work in the UK permanently without extending a visa.
The movement of people from one country or region to another.
The laws and rules a government uses to control who can enter, stay, and settle in a country.
The process of gaining the right to live permanently in a country.
A person whose job requires specific training, experience, or qualifications.
A planned route or sequence of steps that leads to a long-term goal.

sentences.en: Is it becoming harder to move to a new country?
sentences.zh: 移居到一个新的国家是不是变得越来越难了？

sentences.en: Everywhere seems to be tightening the rules.
sentences.zh: 到处似乎都在收紧规则。

sentences.en: Canada, the US, Australia, Europe, Japan, the UK.
sentences.zh: 加拿大、美国、澳大利亚、欧洲、日本、英国。

sentences.en: Countries that once focused on attracting people are now focused on control, limits, and conditions.
sentences.zh: 那些曾经致力于吸引人才的国家，现在把重点转向了控制、限制和条件。

sentences.en: And these changes are happening fast. If you’re thinking about moving to the UK, already living in the UK, or interested in how the world and immigration is changing, I think this episode matters to you.
sentences.zh: 而且这些变化发生得很快。如果你正在考虑移居英国、已经住在英国，或者对世界及移民政策的变化感兴趣，我认为这期节目对你来说很重要。

sentences.en: Because what’s happening in British immigration policy is part of a much bigger global shift.
sentences.zh: 因为英国移民政策中发生的事情，其实是更大范围全球转变的一部分。

sentences.en: Today, we’re going to break down the UK’s new immigration plans.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将详细剖析英国的新移民计划。

sentences.en: We’ll talk about what’s changing, who will be affected, and why these rules are becoming stricter.
sentences.zh: 我们来聊聊哪些在改变、谁会受到影响，以及为什么这些规则变得越来越严。

sentences.en: As this is Thinking in English, I’ll avoid legal jargon, explain everything clearly, and highlight the key vocabulary as we go, so you can understand the policy and improve your English at the same time.
sentences.zh: 既然这是 Thinking in English，我会避开法律术语，把一切解释清楚，并在节目进行中重点讲解核心词汇，这样你既能理解政策，又能同时提升英语水平。

sentences.en: Across many developed countries, populations are aging and birth rates are falling.
sentences.zh: 在许多发达国家，人口正在老龄化，出生率在下降。

sentences.en: Fewer young people are entering the workforce, while more people are retiring.
sentences.zh: 进入劳动力市场的年轻人越来越少，而退休的人越来越多。

sentences.en: On paper, immigration should be the solution or could be one of the solutions to this problem.
sentences.zh: 理论上讲，移民应该是解决这个问题的办法，或者可以成为解决方法之一。

sentences.en: But in reality, immigration has become politically sensitive and a controversial topic in many places.
sentences.zh: 但在现实中，移民在许多地方已经变得政治敏感且极具争议。

sentences.en: Governments are under pressure from voters who are worried about housing shortages, crowded public services, and rising living costs.
sentences.zh: 政府承受着选民的压力，选民们担心住房短缺、公共服务拥挤以及生活成本上升。

sentences.en: When things get more difficult in a country, people often blame immigration.
sentences.zh: 当一个国家的情况变得更加困难时，人们往往会归咎于移民。

sentences.en: For example, when it feels harder to find an apartment or get a job, immigration is an easy target in political debates, even when the causes of these problems are usually much more complex.
sentences.zh: 例如，当觉得找公寓或找工作变难时，在政治辩论中移民就成了一个容易攻击的目标，尽管这些问题产生的原因通常要复杂得多。

sentences.en: Because of this pressure, countries like the UK, Canada, Australia, and several European nations are all tightening their immigration rules at the same time.
sentences.zh: 正因为这种压力，英国、加拿大、澳大利亚和几个欧洲国家都在同时收紧移民规则。

sentences.en: The key shift in many countries is that immigration systems are moving towards something that is more conditional.
sentences.zh: 许多国家的一个关键转变是，移民系统正朝着更加附带条件的方向发展。

sentences.en: Governments are increasingly thinking about what they want potential immigrants to contribute to society, and how long they want immigrants to contribute.
sentences.zh: 政府越来越开始考虑，他们希望潜在移民为社会做出什么贡献，以及他们希望移民贡献多久。

sentences.en: There is a concept that has started to be discussed in the UK recently, and I think it will shape a lot of other countries’ immigration systems too… earned settlement.
sentences.zh: 英国最近开始讨论一个概念，我认为它也将塑造许多其他国家的移民系统……赚取永居权（earned settlement）。

sentences.en: In earned settlement, things like permanent residence and citizenship are not automatic after a number of years.
sentences.zh: 在 earned settlement 这种模式下，永久居留和国籍在几年后不再是自动获得的。

sentences.en: Instead, they are something you have to earn over time.
sentences.zh: 相反，它们是你必须随着时间一点点挣来的。

sentences.en: You can earn your right to live somewhere through work, through paying taxes, through having a high salary, speaking a language, being involved in a community.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过工作、纳税、高薪、说某种语言、参与社区活动，来赢得在某地生活的权利。

sentences.en: And the UK’s new immigration policy fits into this larger global pattern.
sentences.zh: 英国的新移民政策正契合了这一更大的全球趋势。

sentences.en: Once you understand the bigger picture, I think some of the rule changes in the UK start to make more sense.
sentences.zh: 一旦你理解了这幅宏观图景，我认为英国的一些规则变化就开始变得更容易理解了。

sentences.en: In May 2025, the UK published a new immigration white paper.
sentences.zh: 2025年5月，英国发布了一份新的移民白皮书。

sentences.en: A white paper is a government policy document.
sentences.zh: 白皮书是一份政府政策文件。

sentences.en: It explains the government’s plans and their intentions, but it’s not a law yet.
sentences.zh: 它阐述了政府的计划和意图，但还不是法律。

sentences.en: In other words, it shows the direction the government wants to take.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它展现了政府想要采取的方向。

sentences.en: The overall aim of the UK’s new immigration policy is very clear in the white paper: to reduce net migration and to make immigration more selective.
sentences.zh: 英国新移民政策的总体目标在白皮书中非常明确：减少净移民人数，并让移民更具选择性。

sentences.en: To achieve this, the government plans to raise standards across all visas.
sentences.zh: 为了实现这一点，政府计划提高所有签证的门槛。

sentences.en: They want new immigrants to have higher skills, higher incomes, and stronger English language ability.
sentences.zh: 他们希望新移民具备更高的技能、更高的收入和更强的英语能力。

sentences.en: While some of the proposals in this white paper are still being discussed, even as I’m recording this episode, they might have changed since it’s been recorded, others have already been implemented and more changes are scheduled to come into force soon.
sentences.zh: 虽然白皮书中的一些提案仍在讨论中——甚至在我录制这期节目时也是如此，而且自我录制以来它们可能已经发生了变化——但其他一些提案已经付诸实施，还有更多变更计划于近期生效。

sentences.en: The biggest and most controversial change in the UK’s new immigration policy is to do with Indefinite Leave to Remain, often called ILR.
sentences.zh: 英国新移民政策中最大、最具争议的变化与“无限期留英许可”（Indefinite Leave to Remain，通常被称为 ILR）有关。

sentences.en: Indefinite Leave to Remain means that you can live in the UK permanently.
sentences.zh: Indefinite Leave to Remain 意味着你可以在英国永久居住。

sentences.en: You don’t need to extend your visa. You can usually work without restrictions.
sentences.zh: 你不需要延长签证。你通常可以不受限制地工作。

sentences.en: And it’s the final step before applying for British citizenship, if that’s something you want to do.
sentences.zh: 如果你想成为英国公民，这也是申请英国国籍前的最后一步。

sentences.en: For many migrants, ILR has always been the main long-term goal.
sentences.zh: 对许多移民来说，ILR 一直是主要的长期目标。

sentences.en: In some other countries, the equivalent immigration status would be permanent resident or in the US having a green card.
sentences.zh: 在其他一些国家，同等的移民身份是永久居民，或者在美国被称为绿卡。

sentences.en: Under the old UK system ILR was relatively straightforward.
sentences.zh: 在英国旧的体系下，ILR 相对来说比较直接明了。

sentences.en: If you were on most work or family visas, you could usually apply for ILR after five years of living legally in the UK.
sentences.zh: 如果你持有大多数工作签证或家庭签证，在英国合法居住五年后通常就可以申请 ILR。

sentences.en: If you stayed long enough and you followed the rules, settlement was possible.
sentences.zh: 如果你待的时间足够长并且遵守了规则，获得定居身份是有可能的。

sentences.en: It wasn’t particularly difficult. But the UK government is planning to change this significantly.
sentences.zh: 这并不是特别难。但英国政府正计划对此进行重大修改。

sentences.en: And the first changes are coming in April 2026, so just in a few weeks.
sentences.zh: 首批变化将在2026年4月到来，也就是短短几周后。

sentences.en: Under the new policy plans, 10 years will become the baseline for settlement.
sentences.zh: 根据新的政策规划，10年将成为定居的基准线。

sentences.en: A baseline means the standard or default level.
sentences.zh: 基准线意味着标准或默认水平。

sentences.en: So it’s not the maximum or the minimum, but the point from which everything else is measured.
sentences.zh: 所以它既不是上限也不是下限，而是衡量其他一切的标准起点。

sentences.en: Instead of 5 years being the normal waiting period, 10 years will become the starting point.
sentences.zh: 正常等待期将不再是5年，而是以10年作为起点。

sentences.en: This doesn’t mean everyone will have to wait 10 years.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着每个人都必须等上10年。

sentences.en: Some groups are likely to qualify faster, but as of the time I’m writing this, the government has not clarified.
sentences.zh: 某些群体可能会更快符合条件，但截至我写下这些内容时，政府尚未明确说明。

sentences.en: Potentially highly skilled workers, especially those earning higher salaries, or people working in public sector roles like healthcare and teaching, or perhaps people on family visas, especially those who are family members of British citizens, maybe they will be exempt from waiting a full 10 years.
sentences.zh: 潜在的高技能人才，特别是那些收入较高的人，或者在医疗和教学等公共部门角色中工作的人，或者可能是持有家庭签证的人——尤其是英国公民的家庭成员，也许他们可以免除满10年的等待。

sentences.en: But for other immigrants, the waiting time will be much longer.
sentences.zh: 但对其他移民来说，等待时间会长的多。

sentences.en: People in medium skilled jobs could face waiting up to 15 years.
sentences.zh: 从事中等技能工作的人可能面临长达15年的等待。

sentences.en: And refugees, unless they arrive through a specific resettlement program, might have to wait even longer… up to 30 years.
sentences.zh: 而难民，除非通过特定的安置项目抵达，否则可能不得不等待更长时间……长达30年。

sentences.en: Importantly, time alone will no longer be enough to qualify for indefinite leave to remain.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，单靠时间将不再足以满足获得无限期留居许可的条件。

sentences.en: Under the new system, settlement is something you earn, not something you automatically receive.
sentences.zh: 在新系统下，定居是你挣来的，而不是自动获得的。

sentences.en: As I said, we’re still unsure about the specifics, but the UK plans to have a points based system.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，具体细节我们还不是很确定，但英国计划实行积分制。

sentences.en: Things like paying your taxes, earning a high income, volunteering in your local community and speaking advanced English will give you a better chance of being able to stay in the UK permanently.
sentences.zh: 按时纳税、赚取高收入、在当地社区做志愿者以及说一口流利的英语等因素，会给你带来更好的机会留在英国永久居住。

sentences.en: Another clear change in the UK’s immigration policy is the rise in English language requirements.
sentences.zh: 英国移民政策的另一个明显变化是英语语言要求的提高。

sentences.en: For many work-related visas, the required level is increasing from a B1 to a B2 on the CEFR scale.
sentences.zh: 对于许多工作相关签证，所需水平正在从欧洲语言共同参考框架（CEFR）的 B1 提高到 B2。

sentences.en: So basically an increase from intermediate English to upper intermediate.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上是从中级英语提高到中高级。

sentences.en: You will need to understand more complex ideas, explain your opinions more clearly, and be able to communicate confidently.
sentences.zh: 你需要理解更复杂的观点，更清晰地表达你的意见，并且能够自信地沟通。

sentences.en: And it’s not just the main visa holder who will need to speak English.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是主签证持有者需要说英语。

sentences.en: Partners and dependents, so people like husbands, wives, and children of visa holders, will also be affected.
sentences.zh: 伴侣和家属，比如签证持有者的丈夫、妻子和孩子，也将受到影响。

sentences.en: People joining someone already in the UK will now need to show a basic level of English, and if they later want to extend their visa or apply for permanent residence, they will need to prove a higher level again.
sentences.zh: 加入已经在英国的人的家属现在需要展示出基础的英语水平，如果他们以后想要延长签证或申请永久居留权，将需要再次证明达到更高的水平。

sentences.en: The UK is not the only country doing this.
sentences.zh: 英国不是唯一一个这样做的国家。

sentences.en: It’s not the only country considering increasing language proficiency for visa holders.
sentences.zh: 它也不是唯一一个考虑提高签证持有者语言熟练度的国家。

sentences.en: I live in Japan, and it has been widely reported in the media that Japan will be introducing Japanese language requirements for some immigration statuses for the first time.
sentences.zh: 我住在日本，据媒体广泛报道，日本将首次对某些移民身份引入日语语言要求。

sentences.en: There are a number of different reasons why countries care about language.
sentences.zh: 国家之所以重视语言，有许多不同的原因。

sentences.en: The biggest reason is integration. Language is the key to participating in society.
sentences.zh: 最重要的原因是融入。语言是参与社会的钥匙。

sentences.en: If you can’t speak English in the UK, it’s going to be difficult to make friends or understand rules or feel part of the community.
sentences.zh: 如果你在英国不会说英语，你就很难交到朋友、理解规则或融入社区。

sentences.en: Employment is also an important reason. Stronger English ability in the UK is linked to higher productivity and fewer misunderstandings.
sentences.zh: 就业也是一个重要原因。英国更强的英语能力与更高的生产力和更少的误解息息相关。

sentences.en: The weaker your language skills are the less productive you are on average to the economy.
sentences.zh: 你的语言技能越弱，你对经济的平均产出效率就越低。

sentences.en: You’re gonna be earning less money and paying less taxes.
sentences.zh: 你赚的钱会更少，交的税也会更少。

sentences.en: And what the UK government wants is people on higher salaries, paying higher taxes.
sentences.zh: 而英国政府想要的是拿着更高薪水、交着更多税的人。

sentences.en: They don’t want low income immigrants anymore.
sentences.zh: 他们不再想要低收入移民了。

sentences.en: A third reason is public trust. Governments want voters to believe that new immigrants will be able to contribute and communicate and integrate into society.
sentences.zh: 第三个原因是公众信任。政府希望选民相信，新移民将能够为社会做出贡献、进行沟通并融入社会。

sentences.en: Language is the most obvious, the most visible, the most measurable sign of this.
sentences.zh: 语言是最明显、最直观、最可衡量的标志。

sentences.en: Now let’s talk a little bit about work visas, because this is where many of the most immediate changes are happening.
sentences.zh: 现在我们来聊聊工作签证，因为许多最直接的变化就发生在这里。

sentences.en: The skilled worker visa in the UK has become much more restrictive.
sentences.zh: 英国的技术工人签证已经变得限制性极大。

sentences.en: In the past, a wide range of jobs were eligible.
sentences.zh: 过去，各种各样的职业都符合资格。

sentences.en: Now that list is much shorter. Many medium skilled roles have been removed from eligibility.
sentences.zh: 现在这个名单短得多了。许多中等技能的职位已被取消资格。

sentences.en: These are jobs that require training and experience, but not necessarily a university degree.
sentences.zh: 这些工作需要培训和经验，但不一定需要大学学位。

sentences.en: There are still job shortages where sponsorship is possible even without degrees.
sentences.zh: 仍然存在即使没有学位也可以进行担保的人才短缺岗位。

sentences.en: However, these exceptions are temporary.
sentences.zh: 然而，这些例外是临时的。

sentences.en: They’re designed to deal with immediate labor shortages, and they’re not really designed to provide a long-term immigration pathway.
sentences.zh: 它们旨在应对眼前的劳动力短缺，并不是为了提供长期的移民途径。

sentences.en: In some of these cases, people can still come to the UK for work, but they cannot bring dependents.
sentences.zh: 在其中一些情况下，人们仍然可以来英国工作，但不能携带家属。

sentences.en: You cannot bring your husband or your wife or your children.
sentences.zh: 你不能带你的丈夫、妻子或孩子。

sentences.en: For many workers, that makes these visas far less attractive.
sentences.zh: 对于许多工人来说，这使得这些签证的吸引力大打折扣。

sentences.en: Health and care worker visas are also changing, but not in the same way for everyone.
sentences.zh: 健康和护理工人签证也在改变，但对每个人的影响并不完全相同。

sentences.en: The biggest change affects adult social care.
sentences.zh: 最大的变化影响到成人社会护理。

sentences.en: I think recruitment from overseas has already ended or will be ending soon.
sentences.zh: 我认为海外招聘已经结束或即将结束。

sentences.en: This includes jobs like care workers or home support workers.
sentences.zh: 这包括护理员或家庭护工等工作。

sentences.en: Doctors and nurses and other regulated health professionals are obviously not affected by this change.
sentences.zh: 医生、护士和其他受监管的医疗专业人员显然不受此变化影响。

sentences.en: The National Health Service in the UK still relies heavily on overseas staff.
sentences.zh: 英国的国家医疗服务体系（NHS）仍然严重依赖海外员工。

sentences.en: So if you are a skilled doctor, or a nurse or a regulated health professional, something like a physiotherapist or a radiographer, there are still pathways for people like you.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你是一名熟练的医生、护士或是受监管的医疗专业人员（比如理疗师或放射技师），对你这样的人来说仍然有通道。

sentences.en: The overall message from the UK, is that the UK is narrowing the definition of skilled work and closing off some of the pathways that once allowed people to stay and gradually settle.
sentences.zh: 英国传达的总体信息是，英国正在缩小技术工作的定义，并关闭一些曾允许人们留下来并逐步定居的通道。

sentences.en: Many Thinking in English listeners, I think, dream of studying in the UK, so I should probably talk about the changes to student and graduate visas as well.
sentences.zh: 我想很多 Thinking in English 的听众都梦想去英国留学，所以我大概也应该聊聊学生签证和毕业生签证的变化。

sentences.en: For many years immigrants have studied in UK universities with the hope of gaining a job or a career in the UK after graduation.
sentences.zh: 多年来，移民一直在英国大学学习，希望能毕业后在英国找到工作或开启职业生涯。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, the pathway from student to worker is getting increasingly more challenging.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，从学生到工人的转变通道正变得越来越具有挑战性。

sentences.en: One of the biggest changes is the graduate visa.
sentences.zh: 最大的变化之一是毕业生签证。

sentences.en: This is the visa a student is eligible for after they graduate from university.
sentences.zh: 这是学生从大学毕业后有资格获得的签证。

sentences.en: For most students, this visa will be reduced from two years to just 18 months.
sentences.zh: 对大多数学生来说，这种签证的期限将从两年缩短到仅仅18个月。

sentences.en: At the same time, the living cost requirements for students will increase.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，学生的生活成本要求将会提高。

sentences.en: International students must now show they have more money available before they can even apply for a visa.
sentences.zh: 国际学生现在必须证明自己有更多的可用资金，然后才能申请签证。

sentences.en: For many people, this makes studying in the UK more expensive.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，这使得在英国求学的成本更高了。

sentences.en: Moving from a student visa or a graduate visa to a working visa is now harder than it used to be.
sentences.zh: 从学生签证或毕业生签证转为工作签证现在比过去更难了。

sentences.en: Fewer jobs are eligible for sponsorship, and you have to meet high salary thresholds.
sentences.zh: 有资格获得担保的工作变少了，而且你必须满足很高的薪资门槛。

sentences.en: Basically to get a company to sponsor you for work in the UK, you need to earn above the average UK worker, which is not easy to do necessarily as a young student.
sentences.zh: 基本上，要想让公司为你提供在英国工作的担保，你的收入需要高于英国工人的平均水平，作为年轻学生这并不容易做到。

sentences.en: And also employers are much more cautious about sponsoring overseas graduates because it’s expensive.
sentences.zh: 而且雇主在赞助海外毕业生时也更加谨慎，因为这很昂贵。

sentences.en: It’s expensive to sponsor someone. So students are being squeezed from both sides.
sentences.zh: 赞助某人成本很高。所以学生们正面临来自双方面的挤压。

sentences.en: It costs you more to study, and it’s becoming harder to stay afterwards.
sentences.zh: 你学习的花费增加了，而且毕业后留下来也变得越来越难。

sentences.en: Is the UK becoming a temporary study destination rather than a long-term opportunity?
sentences.zh: 英国正在变成一个临时的学习目的地，而不是一个长期的发展机会吗？

sentences.en: Well, maybe? The UK still offers world class universities and great qualifications, but the message is changing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许吧？英国仍然提供世界级的大学和优秀的学历，但传达的信息正在改变。

sentences.en: The UK wants you to study at its universities, but that doesn’t mean it wants you to live or work in the UK after university.
sentences.zh: 英国希望你在其大学学习，但这并不意味着它希望你在大学毕业后在英国生活或工作。

sentences.en: The UK only wants you to stay if you are highly skilled and highly employable.
sentences.zh: 英国只希望你留下来，前提是你高度熟练且具备很强的就业能力。

sentences.en: At this point, I think it’s worth stepping back and considering whether these changes are fair.
sentences.zh: 此时，我认为有必要退一步思考这些变化是否公平。

sentences.en: Across the world, immigration systems are becoming more transactional.
sentences.zh: 在世界各地，移民系统正变得越来越趋向于一种交易。

sentences.en: Migration is increasingly treated like an exchange.
sentences.zh: 移民越来越被当作一种交换。

sentences.en: You bring skills and income and language ability and your labor, and in return, you are given permission to stay.
sentences.zh: 你带来技能、收入、语言能力和你的劳动力，作为回报，你被准许留下来。

sentences.en: If you stop meeting those conditions, your right to remain becomes uncertain.
sentences.zh: 如果你不再满足这些条件，你留下的权利就会变得不确定。

sentences.en: I live in Japan, which is currently considering making major changes to some of its visas.
sentences.zh: 我住在日本，日本目前正在考虑对其部分签证进行重大修改。

sentences.en: They have made it much more difficult to get a business manager visa.
sentences.zh: 他们让获得经营管理签证变得困难得多。

sentences.en: They are considering Japanese language requirements for permanent residents.
sentences.zh: 他们正在考虑对永久居民提出日语语言要求。

sentences.en: They are considering putting limits on certain visa categories to limit the number of people allowed those visas.
sentences.zh: 他们正在考虑对某些签证类别设定限制，以限制获批这些签证的人数。

sentences.en: And they are going to increase the price of visas.
sentences.zh: 而且他们将提高签证的费用。

sentences.en: Several EU countries are also pushing for harder immigration requirements and better border controls.
sentences.zh: 几个欧盟国家也在推动更严苛的移民要求和更好的边境控制。

sentences.en: The UK actually borrowed a lot of these policies from Denmark, which is considered one of the toughest EU countries to move to.
sentences.zh: 英国实际上借鉴了丹麦的许多政策，丹麦被认为是移民难度极高的欧盟国家之一。

sentences.en: Similar to the UK, Canada and Australia are also implementing tighter visa policies, specifically for international students.
sentences.zh: 与英国类似，加拿大和澳大利亚也在实施更严格的签证政策，特别是针对国际学生。

sentences.en: Canada and Australia were famous for being places where you could go to study at university and then relatively easily work there.
sentences.zh: 加拿大和澳大利亚过去以可以去大学读书然后相对容易地在那里工作而闻名。

sentences.en: Now maybe that’s not always the case. And I’m sure you have all seen what’s happening in the US right now on the news, so I won’t talk too much about Donald Trump’s immigration policies.
sentences.zh: 现在情况可能并非总是如此。而且我相信大家最近都在新闻里看到了美国正在发生的事情，所以我不会过多谈论唐纳德·特朗普的移民政策。

sentences.en: From one perspective, the fact these countries are changing their immigration policies makes sense.
sentences.zh: 从某种角度来看，这些国家改变移民政策是有道理的。

sentences.en: Governments want immigration systems that support the economy, protect public services, and do what the people want, what the voters want.
sentences.zh: 政府希望移民系统能够支持经济、保护公共服务，并顺应人民的意愿、选民的意愿。

sentences.en: Prioritizing skills and employment is practical and measurable, but this approach also creates tension.
sentences.zh: 优先考虑技能和就业是务实且可衡量的，但这种方法也带来了紧张局势。

sentences.en: Under the new UK plans, for example, refugees might face a longer path to permanent settlement even though they didn’t always choose to migrate for economic reasons.
sentences.zh: 例如，在英国的新计划下，难民可能会面临更长的永久定居之路，尽管他们迁移并非总是出于经济原因。

sentences.en: Maybe they fled from persecution or danger.
sentences.zh: 也许他们是为了逃离迫害或危险。

sentences.en: Or foreign spouses of UK citizens may need to prove that they have individually earned enough money to pay UK income tax for five years.
sentences.zh: 或者英国公民的外国配偶可能需要证明他们独立赚取了足够的钱来缴纳五年的英国所得税。

sentences.en: Many spouses work part-time or are stay at home parents.
sentences.zh: 许多配偶做兼职或全职在家带孩子。

sentences.en: When I first moved to Japan to live with my wife I didn’t work really for the first three months because I was setting everything up, getting my visa correct, getting my bank account set up.
sentences.zh: 我当初刚搬到日本和妻子一起生活时，前三个月基本上没有工作，因为我在处理所有事情、办妥签证、开立银行账户。

sentences.en: Applying the same “earned settlement” logic to immigrants like spouses can raise some difficult questions, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为，将同样的“赚取永居”逻辑应用到像配偶这样的移民身上，可能会引发一些棘手的问题。

sentences.en: If you are listening to this and thinking about moving to the UK or any country with tightening immigration rules, what should you actually do?
sentences.zh: 如果你正在听这个节目，并考虑移居英国或任何移民规则收紧的国家，你实际上应该怎么做？

sentences.en: Should you give up? No, you shouldn’t. First, you need to plan early.
sentences.zh: 你应该放弃吗？不，你不应该。首先，你需要提前规划。

sentences.en: Immigration systems are changing quickly and they are sometimes changing with little warning.
sentences.zh: 移民系统变化迅速，有时在毫无预警的情况下就会改变。

sentences.en: The earlier you start researching visas and requirements and timelines, the more options you will have.
sentences.zh: 你越早开始研究签证、要求和时间表，你的选择就会越多。

sentences.en: Second, don’t aim for the minimum. What I mean is… don’t aim for the minimum income requirement for a visa or the minimum English language requirement for a visa.
sentences.zh: 其次，不要只瞄准最低标准。我的意思是……不要把目标定在签证的最低收入要求或最低英语语言要求上。

sentences.en: If a government plans to change something, it’s likely they’re going to make it more difficult.
sentences.zh: 如果一个政府计划改变什么，他们很可能会让事情变得更困难。

sentences.en: So having a higher salary or a higher English ability gives you more flexibility.
sentences.zh: 因此，拥有更高的薪水或更好的英语能力能给你带来更大的灵活性。

sentences.en: Third, make sure you understand the long-term settlement pathways, not just your first visa.
sentences.zh: 第三，确保你理解长期的定居途径，而不仅仅是你的第一个签证。

sentences.en: Many people focus on getting into a country, but the challenge is staying.
sentences.zh: 许多人专注于进入一个国家，但真正的挑战是留下来。

sentences.en: Look closely at how long settlement takes, what conditions apply, and what could affect your immigration status.
sentences.zh: 仔细研究定居需要多长时间、适用什么条件，以及什么因素可能会影响你的移民身份。

sentences.en: I’ve seen this a lot with my friends and with myself personally.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友们和我自己身上都经常看到这种情况。

sentences.en: I was in Tokyo four years ago on a student visa.
sentences.zh: 四年前我在东京持学生签证。

sentences.en: I was a research student at a university and my visa was ending.
sentences.zh: 我是一所大学的研究生，我的签证快到期了。

sentences.en: Thinking in English was really at the early stages, and I couldn’t stay in Japan.
sentences.zh: Thinking in English 当时正处于初期阶段，我无法留在日本。

sentences.en: Because there was no way to move from a student visa to a self-employed visa.
sentences.zh: 因为根本没有办法从学生签证转为自雇签证。

sentences.en: That doesn’t exist in Japan. So I had to leave and I came back a few months later married.
sentences.zh: 日本没有这种途径。所以我不得不离开，几个月后我结了婚又回来了。

sentences.en: I have friends who’ve done something similar.
sentences.zh: 我有朋友做过类似的事情。

sentences.en: Studied abroad, and then they have to leave there’s no route from student to worker perhaps.
sentences.zh: 在海外留学，然后不得不离开，也许根本没有从学生转为工人的途径。

sentences.en: Or people who have done a short term tourist visa with the hope of living or working somewhere, and they realize working on a tourist visa is almost always illegal, and if you get caught, you will never be able to live in that country again.
sentences.zh: 或者有人拿着短期旅游签证，抱着在某地生活或工作的希望，结果发现持旅游签证工作几乎总是非法的，如果你被抓到，你将再也无法在这个国家生活。

sentences.en: You also should never assume that the rules you see today will still be the same rules tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 你还应该永远不要假设你今天看到的规则明天还会保持不变。

sentences.en: Immigration policy is political and governments adjust their systems in response to public pressure and elections and economic conditions.
sentences.zh: 移民政策具有政治性，政府会根据公众压力、选举和经济状况来调整他们的系统。

sentences.en: In January, Donald Trump banned 75 countries from applying for visas to the USA.
sentences.zh: 在一月份，唐纳德·特朗普禁止了75个国家的公民申请美国签证。

sentences.en: These were not just the typical countries you might expect Trump to ban.
sentences.zh: 这些不仅仅是你可能预料到特朗普会禁止的典型国家。

sentences.en: They also included places that were maybe his rivals, places like Brazil, or I think Uruguay was on that list as well.
sentences.zh: 它们还包括可能是他的竞争对手的地方，比如巴西，或者我想乌拉圭也在那个名单上。

sentences.en: You can’t assume what you see today will still be in place tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 你不能假设你今天看到的明天依然存在。

sentences.en: Moving internationally is still possible.
sentences.zh: 国际间的大规模流动依然是可能的。

sentences.en: Thousands of people, millions of people do it every year, but you need to be aware of the changes in the immigration systems.
sentences.zh: 成千上万、数以百万计的人每年都在这样做，但你需要意识到移民系统的变化。

sentences.en: If you are proficient in the language of the country you want to move to and you have skills or abilities that the country needs or wants, then you have an amazing chance at moving.
sentences.zh: 如果你精通你想移居的国家的语言，并且拥有该国需要或想要的技能或能力，那么你就有绝佳的机会移居。

sentences.en: You have a great chance. If you are a highly skilled person in your industry.
sentences.zh: 你会有很大的机会。如果你是你所在行业的高技能人才。

sentences.en: If you have experience, if you are respected in your industry, if you have connections, if you can prove that you will be beneficial to a country, then yes, people will hire you.
sentences.zh: 如果你有经验、在行业内受人尊重、有人脉，如果你能证明自己对一个国家有益，那么是的，人们会雇用你的。

sentences.en: There are jobs out there. There are jobs hiring internationally all the time.
sentences.zh: 外面有很多工作机会。随时都有在国际上招人的工作。

sentences.en: I have friends living in countries across the world, but you need to have those skills.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友们住在世界各地的国家，但你需要具备这些技能。

sentences.en: It’s no longer just enough to think, “oh, I want to move to the UK “.
sentences.zh: 光是想着“哦，我想搬到英国”已经不够了。

sentences.en: You have to think, “what are you going to contribute?” “How are you going to convince someone to hire you after you graduate from a degree?”
sentences.zh: 你必须思考：“你能贡献什么？”“你毕业拿到学位后，要如何说服别人雇佣你？”

sentences.en: But what do you think? Are you living abroad?
sentences.zh: 但你怎么看？你现在住在海外吗？

sentences.en: Do you want to live abroad? How about your country?
sentences.zh: 你想住在海外吗？你的国家呢？

sentences.en: Is your country accepting immigrants or not really wanting immigrants right now?
sentences.zh: 你的国家现在是接受移民还是不太欢迎移民？
